claims.text: The as-cast magnetic high-entropy alloy has a relatively homogeneous, single-phase microstructure.
Thermal aging can induce finely dispersed nanoscale precipitates in the magnetic high-entropy alloy.
A treatment near 500 °C for 2 hours in an inert atmosphere is suitable for producing the proposed precipitate microstructure.
Aging will form coherent or semi-coherent nanoscale precipitates distributed throughout the matrix and particularly at or near grain boundaries.
The nanoscale precipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Precipitate-induced pinning impedes magnetic domain-wall motion.
Greater domain-wall pinning raises the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
The increased barrier to domain-wall motion increases the coercive field.
The aged alloy will have a higher room-temperature, quasi-static coercive field than a matched as-cast alloy.
The proposed coercivity increase requires the precipitates to remain thermally stable and uniformly distributed.
Extreme temperatures or very high magnetic measurement frequencies may change the effectiveness of precipitate-mediated domain-wall pinning.
Precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction depend on the alloy and on the selected aging temperature and duration.
